claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your Child Benefit eligibility! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about your child or children.

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

To help me guide you through the eligibility check, I need to know:
- **The child's age** (or if you have multiple children, their ages)

Please let me know the age(s) so I can continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit and wanted to check if I'm eligible. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 8 years old, which means Alex falls into the **under 16 category**.

Let me continue with the eligibility assessment for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! Since Alex is under 16, I just need to check one more thing:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is Alex not in paid work at all?**

(This is a standard check for all children - most under 16s won't be working full-time anyway, but I need to confirm this to proceed.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8, so he's just in primary school!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's what I expected for an 8-year-old. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?** 

Specifically, is Alex not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

(For an 8-year-old in school, the answer is almost certainly "yes" - they wouldn't be receiving these - but I need to confirm.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's just a regular 8-year-old!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check about apprenticeships. Though at 8 years old this is unlikely:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship of any kind?**

(Given Alex is 8 and in primary school, the answer should be "no" - but I need to confirm to proceed.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - he's only 8! He's just in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's exactly what I expected. Let me move forward with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check your residency requirements. This is an important part of the eligibility assessment.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

Or do you fall into any of these special circumstances:
- You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with specific working/seeking work/resources requirements)
- You're studying or a family member of an EEA/Swiss national
- You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries

For most people, the answer is simply "yes, I normally live in the UK." Could you let me know your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's straightforward then. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means either:
1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** (paying for food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc. - at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount), OR
3. **You're paying maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Which applies to your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That's clear then - you live with Alex. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check something important:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- The other parent
- A grandparent
- Another carer

Or is Alex only claimed for by you (or no one currently)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Is Alex currently:**
- Living at home normally with you, OR
- In hospital, OR
- In local authority care, OR
- Fostered with someone else?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home normally with me - just a regular situation.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the final checks.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

(In other words, you're paying for Alex's housing and care yourself - not through a council arrangement?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - I pay for everything myself. The council isn't paying for anything.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I have all the information I need. Let me provide you with your eligibility outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful news! Now let me record your eligibility outcome formally.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ Great News - You're Eligible!

**You are ELIGIBLE to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

### Summary:
You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit:
- ✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time
- ✅ Alex is not receiving benefits in their own name
- ✅ Alex is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship
- ✅ You live in the UK (Manchester)
- ✅ You are responsible for Alex (living at home with you)
- ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✅ Alex is living at home normally
- ✅ The council is not paying for Alex's accommodation/maintenance

### Next Steps - How to Claim:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit or **by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of:**
   - Your identity
   - Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important Note:** Be aware of the **High Income Child Benefit Charge** - if you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay tax on the benefit

4. **Payment Schedule:** Child Benefit is paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Good luck with your claim!

reasonings: Alex is 8 years old (under 16, automatically qualifying), not working full-time, not receiving benefits in their own name, not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. You live in the UK (Manchester) and are responsible for Alex as they live at home with you. No other person is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. Alex is living at home normally (not in hospital, care, or fostered), and the local council is not paying for Alex's accommodation or maintenance. All eligibility criteria are met.
arguments.overall_reasoning: You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex. As a single parent living in Manchester with your 8-year-old child who lives at home with you, you meet all the eligibility requirements. You should now proceed with making a claim.">
